answer.question: What should I check before turf installation in Atlantic Beach?
answer.answer: The City publishes turf-installation guidance covering product information, base preparation, trees and inspection. Ask which requirements apply to your property and proposed system, including lot coverage. Plan any required inspection before the turf covers the base.

blocks.h2: Choose putting lines, pet access or everyday lawn space.
paras: In an established Atlantic Beach yard, keep the patio routes and mature trees in the plan. A green near the house can be designed around useful putts and walking room. A pet area needs cleaning access and a routine as well as a finished edge.

blocks.h2: Do not bury a base that still needs inspection.
paras: Atlantic Beach’s published guidance calls for product and permeability documentation, installation details and inspection of the exposed base. Confirm the currently applicable requirements with the City before materials are ordered or work is covered.

Its guidance also addresses work around trees, the public right-of-way and preserving drainage. Identify those features on the property plan. Ask how the proposed complete system counts toward lot coverage, particularly when other hard surfaces already use much of the lot.

blocks.h2: Atlantic Beach writes down how turf goes in, then checks the base.
paras: Atlantic Beach publishes formal Artificial Turf Installation Guidelines, and they're specific (City of Atlantic Beach). The turf needs ASTM-certified permeability of at least 100 inches per hour. Under it goes a free-draining stone base at least 4 inches deep: 2 inches of #57 stone as the drainage layer, with 2 inches of #89 on top, or clean angular crushed rock with little or no fines.
The product must be free of hazardous materials and heavy metals. Turf can't go in the city right-of-way, and it can't change drainage patterns or push runoff onto a neighboring property.
Then the city checks the work. The stone base has to be inspected and approved before any turf covers it, so it stays open until the city signs off. Nothing gets buried before it's been seen.

blocks.h2: Confirm how the proposed surface counts toward lot coverage.
paras: Since Ordinance 90-19-238 in February 2019, homes in the city's conventional residential districts have been capped at 45% impervious cover, down from 50%, and swimming pools count toward it (News4Jax). Development that takes a lot past 35% impervious coverage also has to store its own stormwater on site, with a cumulative 400-square-foot exemption (Atlantic Beach code).

A patio, a driveway extension or a pool spends that allowance. Confirm the proposed turf system’s classification with the city before assuming that it leaves the impervious allowance unchanged. The city tightened the cap to deal with stormwater and flooding (Beaches Leader), and a base that drains is the whole point.

Since 19 May 2026, state law has also barred cities from banning turf on a single-family lot, or regulating it inconsistently with the state standard (Florida Statutes 125.572). Where the city's guidelines and the state's differ for your lot, ask the city in writing which it applies. Our impervious surface guide has the wider picture.

blocks.h2: Under a live oak, the guidelines keep turf back from the trunk.
paras: Old Atlantic Beach and Selva Marina sit under mature live oaks, with heavy shade and protected root zones, which is why the city's guidelines carry tree rules. Keep turf outside the drip line where you can. Under one, stay at least 18 to 24 inches from the trunk, keep the base no deeper than 3 inches, compact it lightly, and keep everything permeable to water and oxygen, with no pooling at the foot of the tree.

Discuss the ground, drainage and tree-root constraints at the actual work area. A turf surface alone does not establish a drainage solution or a lot-coverage exemption. Shade is also part of the layout discussion; read about turf and heat before choosing a play or pet area.

faq.q: Who installs artificial turf in Atlantic Beach, FL?
faq.a: Timeless installs artificial lawns, pet turf and backyard putting greens in Atlantic Beach, FL. The city publishes turf-installation guidance. Check which requirements and surface classification apply to your property and proposed system before finalizing the plan. Start with a free visit, layout and written price.

faq.q: What does Atlantic Beach ask for before the turf goes in?
faq.a: The manufacturer's product specifications, permeability test documentation, installation details or cross-section drawings, and a site plan showing the turf against your trees and property lines (City of Atlantic Beach). Then the city inspects the exposed base before any turf is laid.

faq.q: Can I use paver sand under turf in Atlantic Beach?
faq.a: No. The city's guidelines prohibit paver sand, crushed fines, stone screenings, decomposed granite containing fines, and any compacted material that reduces permeability, and they allow light compaction only (City of Atlantic Beach). A base made that way fails the city's inspection.

faq.q: Can turf go in the drainage or retention area on my lot?
faq.a: In a privately owned stormwater retention or drainage area, only if its designed storage volume and drainage still work, with nothing blocking structures, overflow paths or maintenance access (City of Atlantic Beach). The city may ask for engineering documents to prove it.

faq.q: Who supplies water in Atlantic Beach, and when can I water?
faq.a: The city's own Public Utilities Department, not JEA (City of Atlantic Beach utilities). Under the Phase III order in force since May 2026, a lawn gets a single day's watering a week, odd addresses on Saturday and even on Sunday, outside a daytime ban from 8 a.m. until 6 p.m., and private wells are included (St. Johns River Water Management District). Micro-irrigation and hand-held hoses are exempt.
